records.found: On 2026-11-05 Cell Stem Cell published a paper (online) on DNA-methylation epigenome editing of one gene (ITGB3) in human blood-forming stem cells, with silencing still present four months after transplant into mice; this is cells and mice, not a person. The registry entry for the hepatitis B trial (NCT06671093) was last updated 2026-01-06 and is unchanged; I found no new company release or peer-reviewed human report in the window. Older fact the entry lacks: Epicrispr's release of 2026-01-08 on a first-in-human epigenetic editing study in a muscle disease (not opened, 403).

findings.what: Cell Stem Cell: durable, reversible epigenetic silencing in primary human blood stem cells, stable 4 months after transplant into mice (abstract read via Europe PMC)
Registry entry NCT06671093 last updated; status recruiting; primary completion 2028-06-28; no results posted
Epicrispr release: early clinical activity in first-in-human epigenetic editing study (EPI-321) for a muscle disease; not read

records.found: Acumen announced on 2026-10-30 (three days before the window) that its amyloid antibody sabirnetug missed the main measure in a phase 2 trial of 542 people despite clearing plaque, and stopped development; trade press covered it on 2026-11-03. On 2026-11-04 a German pharmacists' journal reported a neurologist's estimate that 1,000 to 2,000 people had been treated in Germany in a year and that the German assessors found no proven added benefit; this weighs against the 2035 wide-use year (weakly, as it is one doctor's estimate) and the antibody class's record of plaque clearing without clear gain.

findings.what: NeurologyLive report: sabirnetug missed primary endpoint (iADRS at 18 months); plaque reduced; Acumen ceasing development. Company release dated 2026-10-30
Pharmazeutische Zeitung (dpa): about a year of lecanemab and donanemab in Germany; estimate of 1,000 to 2,000 treated; no proven added benefit per the German assessors; price talks ongoing
Neurological Sciences paper: amyloid PET at 52 weeks as cost-effective way to guide duration-limited donanemab treatment (abstract via Europe PMC)
